item.title: Apple and Google Explore AI Cameras That Don't Record Video
item.description:
Apple and Google Explore AI Cameras That Don’t Record Video

Apple is reportedly working on a smart home camera that does not save video recordings. Instead, AI processes the visual data to generate text snippets describing activity. This concept is also being considered by Google for smart glasses.

🔍 Overview

Last week, Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman reported that Apple is working on a smart home camera that doesn’t save video recordings. Instead, AI uses the visual data to create text snippets that describe what’s happening around your home. Supposedly, it’ll support facial recognition, but without video footage. This tech, Gurman says, is similar to how the cameras in rumored future AirPods will also work.

🧩 How It Works

The system relies on processing data locally and discarding raw footage:

  • The camera processes visual data using AI but does not save video footage.
  • Raw data is deleted once it finishes processing in a separate, secure exclave on the S11 processor.
  • Any information sent to the cloud is through private cloud compute and is therefore inaccessible to Apple or third parties.
  • Apple says these features don’t save any audio.

⚙️ Key Details

  • This approach is similar to Apple’s Audio Intelligence on the Apple Watch Series 12 and Apple Watch Ultra 4.
  • Of the four Audio Intelligence features, two have caused the most debate online: Live Rewind and Siri Recap.
  • Live Rewind produces a transcript of the past 15 seconds, whereas Siri Recap can generate high-level summaries of the conversations you have throughout the day.
  • Google is also mulling this concept. Sandeep Waraich, Google’s senior director of wearables, asked: “What if… cameras on smart glasses didn’t record data?” He argued the camera could “just” be an image sensor.

💡 Why It Matters

The shift away from storing recordings raises new questions about privacy and transparency:

  • Preserved snippets: Even if no video is saved, text transcripts generated by a smart home camera or smartwatch could still count as preserved and reviewable data.
  • Indicator confusion: Apple uses a white, pulsing “privacy light” to indicate recording. However, the universal color for recording is red, so a less tech-savvy person may not know what a white light signifies. White lights are also easily obscured by bangs and bright sunlight.
  • Inconsistent norms: Other smart glasses or AI hardware companies aren’t obligated to signal intent like Meta. An AI ring or pendant that records audio or video may have no light at all.
  • Form factor ambiguity: Products that can record increasingly look like products that can’t. For example, an Oura Ring (no microphone) looks like a Vocci Ring (with microphone), and both look like regular rings.
  • The real issue: The queasy feeling comes from knowing a preserved snippet of you can exist in someone else’s device with no knowledge of how it’ll be used — not just from the camera or microphone itself.

#Apple #Google #AIprivacy #smarthome #wearables

Source: We can’t just change the definition of ‘recording’

item.title: Meta Introduces Muse AI Agent for Smart Glasses and Charm Wearable
item.description:
Meta Introduces Muse AI Agent for Smart Glasses and Charm Wearable

Meta has introduced Muse, an AI agent designed to assist users with productivity, health, and relationship goals.

⚙️ Key details

Muse features a mascot named “Jolly,” described as a pink-cheeked character with plush ivory fur. Depending on the context, the agent’s appearance and persona can vary:

Version/Instance Description
Jolly The official mascot seen in various outfits on campus cutouts.
Cooper Meta CTO Andrew Bosworth’s agent, dressed as a test pilot.
Henry An audio-only version with the tones of a British man, designed to assist a fictional 38-year-old gym bro named Sean.

🧩 How it works

Users can interact with Muse through smart glasses to assist with decision-making based on personal context, such as viewing an object and receiving AI guidance. The agent can also learn from user data, such as emails, to alter its appearance.

Capabilities and observed performance include:

  • Health Guidance: Providing workout regimens for goals such as regaining muscle and achieving a sub-30 minute 5K.
  • Contextual Analysis: Evaluating snacks for protein content relative to calories.
  • Limitations: In demonstrations, the agent mistakenly reported incorrect protein grams for a protein bar and failed to add granola bites to a cart because the product “did not exist in the catalog.”

🚀 Availability

Muse is being integrated into the following hardware:

  • All of Meta’s smart glasses.
  • Charm, a new standalone AI wearable described as part chunky smartwatch, part Humane AI Pin, and part Tamagotchi.

#Meta #Muse #AIagents #Wearables #SmartGlasses

Source: It’s sinister that Meta’s Muse AI mascot is so cute

item.title: Streamlined Edge ML Workflow for WeBe Band Wearable Device
item.description:
Streamlined Edge ML Workflow for WeBe Band Wearable Device

Researchers have developed a streamlined edge ML workflow to enable the rapid development, optimization, and deployment of machine-learning models directly on the WeBe Band, a wrist-worn device for multimodal physiological data monitoring.

🧩 How it works

The system focuses on system-level automation and deployability, integrating the open-source Piccolo AI ecosystem with an automated pipeline. This framework provides the following capabilities:

  • Hardware-aware model compilation
  • Generation of deployable firmware artifacts
  • Support for over-the-air (OTA) deployment
  • Hardware-aware quantization and AutoML
  • Performance profiling to meet latency targets within device memory and power limitations

⚙️ Key details

The workflow supports multiple lightweight model classes and provides on-device profiling tools to evaluate memory footprint and inference latency under realistic conditions.

Model Class Performance Observations
Classical machine-learning algorithms Offer strong real-time performance
Neural networks Require careful resource management

💡 Why it matters

This work enables researchers and developers to rapidly iterate on models and evaluate them directly on target hardware. While demonstrated on the WeBe Band platform, the workflow is designed to be extensible to other ML-powered edge devices.

#EdgeML #Wearables #AutoML #EmbeddedSystems

Source: A Rapid Pipeline for Training and Deploying ML Models on WeBe Band
